THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The registration of the FIR for the offences punishable under sections 406 and 420 of IPC is impugned in this petition.

2. The 2nd respondent lodged the FIR alleging that he was the tenant of the subject property belonging to the petitioner and a settlement was arrived between the petitioner and the 2nd respondent, and in terms of the settlement, the 2nd respondent handed over the subject premises to the petitioner and the petitioner had agreed to pay a sum of Rs.2,75,00,000/- towards investment of furniture and other furniture wood works made by the 2nd respondent.

3. In terms of the settlement arrived between the parties, the petitioner issued two post dated cheques for a sum of Rs.2,75,00,000/- and when the said cheques were presented for realization,
the same was dishonoured for want of funds.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the cheques were not honoured on the instructions made by the petitioner to make stop payment since the furniture and the woodwork were hypothecated to the Canara Bank by the 2nd NC: 2023:KHC:40982 respondent towards repayment of the loan borrowed by him, and suppressing the same, the 2nd respondent entered into an agreement of settlement.

Therefore, he submits that in the absence of any allegation that the petitioner induced the 2nd respondent to enter into an agreement of settlement with an intention to cheat, the registration of the FIR for the offence of cheating is impermissible.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submits that the allegations made in the FIR discloses the commission of the cognizable offence and the veracity of the allegations requires to be investigated and at this stage, the registration of the FIR does not warrant any interference.

sentences.text: Considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties.

7. Settlement agreement dated 6.11.2021 annexed to this petition at Annexure-C indicated that, the tenant had handed over the possession to the landlord and in terms of the settlement, the petitioner landlord had agreed to pay a sum of Rs.2,75,00,000/- to the 2nd respondent towards the value of the furniture and woodwork.

To honour the said payment, the petitioner had issued two post dated cheques and when the said cheques presented for realization were dishonored on the instructions given to the Bank by the petitioner to make stop payment of the said cheques, since the furniture and the NC: 2023:KHC:40982 woodwork were hypothecated to the Canara Bank by the 2nd respondent towards repayment of the loan borrowed by him.
8. To constitute an offence punishable under Sections 406 & 420 of IPC, a person must have entrusted the property, and the property so entrusted, must have been mis- appropriated, and the person must have been induced to enter into an agreement with an intention to cheat.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarabjit Kaur v State of Punjab & Others has held that breach of contract does not give rise to criminal prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right at the beginning of the transaction.

entities.text: Sarabjit Kaur v State of Punjab & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In the instant case, there are no allegations that the petitioner induced the 2nd respondent to enter into an agreement of settlement with an intention of cheating.
Moreover, the furniture and woodwork is attached by the Bank for recovering the loan amount borrowed by the informant.

Therefore, in the absence of essential elements to constitute the commission of the aforesaid offences, the registration of the FIR is impermissible and the continuation of the investigation against the petitioner-accused herein will be an abuse of process of law.
Accordingly, I pass the following:

ORDER i) The criminal petition is allowed;
NC: 2023:KHC:40982 ii) The impugned FIR in Crime No.74/2022, registered by the Kadugodi Police Station, Bengaluru City is hereby quashed.

iii) Any observations made in this order will not come in the way of the Trial Court in adjudicating the claim of the parties including the proceedings for the offence under the provision of the N.I. Act.

Sd/-
JUDGE HR Lokesh Kumar.
